overview: In Jainism, 'Hierarchy' refers to the structured organization of spiritual authority and practices within the tradition. Jainism does not have a centralized religious authority like a pope, but it has a well-defined hierarchy of spiritual leaders and practitioners. The hierarchy is typically based on levels of spiritual advancement and adherence to Jain principles. This includes monks and nuns, who are considered higher in spiritual hierarchy due to their renunciation of worldly life, followed by householders who practice Jain principles while leading a family life. The concept of hierarchy also extends to the categorization of beings based on their level of consciousness, ranging from one-sensed beings to the fully liberated souls, known as Siddhas. This hierarchical classification informs ethical conduct and spiritual practices, emphasizing non-violence and compassion towards all living beings.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: Right perception, right knowledge, and right conduct constitute the path to liberation.
primary_sources.notes: This text outlines the path to liberation, emphasizing a structured approach to spiritual advancement.

misconceptions.myth: Jain hierarchy is similar to a rigid caste system.
misconceptions.reality: While Jain hierarchy involves levels of spiritual advancement, it is based on personal spiritual progress and practices, not birth or caste.
